reading: The proposal changes one recorded relation: the Mill Compact's purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild in every season, not only under Alternative B (E11, E3). Of 55 mechanism items, 51 are preserved, E11 is transformed and E32-E34 are historical, so the recorded change is confined to this relation (E1). The preserved statements that purchased draw carries no return labour (E19, E63) now sit beside it. Later dependence is not recorded; the reach is long-horizon because the rebuild node it feeds is one the Long Return needs channel labour from (E51).

concerns.title: Compact draw stated two ways
concerns.reading: The changed relation (E11, proposed side E3) says purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild in every season, where the baseline tied it to Alternative B. The preserved node text (E19) and the preserved trade link (E63) still say purchased draw carries no return labour, and all three meet at inst_mill_compact. Whether return labour in E63 is the same labour as the rebuild duty is not stated. That is an interpretation for the owner to check, not a finding.

concerns.title: Trade and draw links kept
concerns.reading: The link that opens records to trade (E47) is preserved, and the Compact's draw link to the Source keeps its text (E63). The change adds a labour relation at the Compact and does not state that it alters draw. Whether it does is not established; this is an interpretation of unchanged text.

concerns.title: Open question on the Compact's exchange
concerns.reading: Open question q-compact-settlement keeps the same wording in both candidates. It asks whether the Compact accepts grain-labour in exchange for settling its claim, and it is recorded as not decided. The changed relation (E11) makes the labour a standing duty with no exchange stated, so the question's premise may be displaced rather than answered. E8 places the Compact's bid in Books 27-29, which the packet does not show in text.

concerns.title: Alternative B's grain-labour clause
concerns.reading: Alternative B's record names grain-labour from the Compact as one of its terms (E13). Once the Compact owes that labour in every season (E11), the labour no longer marks B. B keeps its rota, lot-drawn Table seats and sunset, but its Compact clause loses a distinct role. This is an interpretation of two texts.

concerns.title: Long Return's channel labour
concerns.reading: The Long Return is a Book 30 pulse that needs channel labour before its date (E26, E51). The changed relation gives the rebuild Compact labour in every season (E11), so that labour could be available before Alternative B is activated. The shared rebuild node is recorded; that the pulse depends on Compact labour is not, and is hypothetical.

concerns.title: Alternative A's nothing-owed wording
concerns.reading: Alternative A says draw is decoupled from hands and nothing is owed (E12). Under Alternative C, normal seasons follow A (E37), and the changed relation still has the Compact owing labour in those seasons (E11). Whether 'nothing is owed' reaches an outside buyer such as the Compact is not stated. The wording may be displaced in scope; it is not shown to be contradicted.

mechanisms.reading: Transformed (E11, changed_fields: function): the scope 'under B' is removed and 'in every season' is added. Endpoints inst_mill_compact and th_maintenance are unchanged; the proposed record is E3. Interpretation: the Compact becomes a standing supplier to the rebuild, not a supplier only under B.

Preserved (E19): 'Their purchased draw carries no return labour' is unchanged. Beside the transformed relation (E11), the node text no longer matches that relation's scope. The record does not say which governs. Interpretation only.

Preserved (E63): 'purchased shares draw without return labour' from inst_mill_compact to eng_source is unchanged in text. It shares the Compact node with the transformed relation, so two statements about the Compact's labour meet there. Whether they conflict depends on what return labour means in each.

Preserved (E13): B's record names grain-labour from the Compact as a term. The transformed relation (E11) gives that labour in every season, so the term no longer defines B alone. Interpretation: B's labour clause now restates a standing duty.

Preserved (E12): 'care is counted and nothing is owed' is unchanged. A governs normal seasons under C (E37), where the transformed relation still has the Compact owing labour (E11). Whether 'nothing is owed' reaches the Compact is not stated.

Preserved (E31): the summary says lineage crews carry repair from Book 20 and households that can meet the rota carry the rest. The transformed relation (E11) adds a standing Compact source the summary does not name. Interpretation: the summary may understate maintenance sources.

inheritance.text: Not established. Books 24 and 25 cite th_maintenance (E70, E74), but no shown element cites inst_mill_compact or the changed relation. Most considered elements are omitted from the packet, so this is not evidence that the change is absent.

Not recorded. Suggested construction: a Book 27-29 Compact-bid element that cites the changed relation, so that a later Book carries the standing duty explicitly. Whether to build it is the author's decision.

trajectories.title: Standing Compact labour meets the Long Return

steps.text: The transformed relation supplies Compact grain-labour to th_maintenance in every season (E11), and the Long Return needs channel labour from th_maintenance before its date (E51).
In Books 27-29 the Compact's bid may be framed against a standing labour duty rather than a term of B (E8, E19). This step is not recorded.
In Book 30 the pulse's channel labour may be partly met by Compact labour before its date, so the choice among A, B and C would start from a different labour baseline. This step is not recorded.

alternatives.title: Keep the Compact's labour tied to Alternative B
alternatives.summary: The Compact's grain-labour stays a duty under Alternative B only, as the baseline records it, and the open question keeps its exchange framing. The proposed standing duty is not adopted, and the rest of the record is unchanged.
alternatives.gains: Keeps the statements that purchased draw carries no return labour (E19, E63) free of a conflicting standing duty, keeps A's nothing-owed wording unqualified, and keeps B's Compact clause distinct.
alternatives.costs: The rebuild gets no Compact labour until B is activated, so the Long Return's channel labour (E51) must come from households and lineage crews, and the baseline does not show that they can meet it.
alternatives.next_investigation: Read the Compact's Book 27-29 bid and the Book 30 routing to see whether either needs labour before B is activated.

alternatives.title: Accept the standing Compact labour duty as written
alternatives.summary: The Compact owes grain-labour to the rebuild in every season, as the proposed relation states. The displacement it causes is recorded as accepted, not resolved: the no-labour statements (E19, E63), the open question's exchange framing (its wording is unchanged, so it stays not decided), and the distinct clause in Alternative B.
alternatives.gains: Gives the rebuild a standing source of channel labour that does not depend on Alternative B's activation, so the Long Return's labour need (E51) could be met earlier.
alternatives.costs: Two recorded statements about the Compact's labour stay unchanged and conflict with the relation. The exchange question stays not decided while its premise is displaced. Alternative B's grain-labour clause loses its B-specific role.
alternatives.next_investigation: Decide whether 'owes' conditions purchased draw, then check the Book 27-29 bid for a standing duty and whether E19 and E63 need revision.

alternatives.title: Separate the standing duty from the settlement
alternatives.summary: Split the baseline question in two. One part is the standing grain-labour duty the proposal records for every season. The other is a settlement the Compact may negotiate for its claim, which the baseline question still asks. A distinct new question, whether the standing duty is itself a settlement, is described here and not given an identity.
alternatives.gains: Records the standing labour without deciding the settlement, and keeps the exchange framing available for the Compact's Book 27-29 bid.
alternatives.costs: Two relations would answer one baseline question, and the record must explain how the standing duty relates to the settlement. Alternative B's Compact clause stays displaced unless it is addressed separately.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check whether Books 27-29 treat the Compact's labour as a standing duty or as a term of its settlement. The packet gives that bid only at phase level.

connections.text: Both links leave inst_mill_compact, a shared node. The transformed relation says purchased draw owes labour in every season (E11), while the preserved trade link says purchased shares draw without return labour (E63). The proposed candidate holds both statements at one node.
counterevidence: The packet does not say whether return labour in E63 is the rebuild labour named in E11.

connections.text: Both meet at th_maintenance. The transformed relation supplies Compact labour to the rebuild every season (E11), and the Long Return link says the pulse needs channel labour before its date (E51). The shared node is recorded; a supply-to-need dependency is not.
counterevidence: The Long Return link does not name the Compact or any labour source.

connections.text: Not recorded as linked. Alternative B's record names grain-labour from the Compact (E13), and the transformed relation names the same labour as a standing duty (E11). The two texts appear to describe one labour supply at different scopes.
connections.reasoning: Both texts name grain-labour owed to the rebuild by the Compact, so the labour is likely the same; the difference is scope (E11 every season, E13 within the rebuild window under B).
assumptions: The grain-labour in E13 and in E11 is the same labour.
The proposal changes nothing else in Alternative B's record.
counterevidence: B's rota and window differ from the standing duty, so the labour may not be a single supply.

not_established: Whether Books 26-30 depend on the changed relation: the packet gives Book content for Books 24 and 25 only, and the Compact's Book 27-29 bid appears only at phase level.

Whether Books 24-25 carry the change: 100 of 124 considered Book elements are omitted, no shown element cites inst_mill_compact or the changed relation, and none records a decision on the examined questions.
Whether 'owes' in the changed relation conditions purchased draw, or names only a labour duty to the rebuild: the packet does not say.
Whether Compact grain-labour and lineage channel repair draw on the same labour, and whether standing Compact labour could meet the Long Return's need before Alternative B is activated: not recorded.
Whether the Compact would accept a standing duty in place of the exchange the baseline question asks about: q-compact-settlement stays recorded as not decided.
Whether 'nothing is owed' in Alternative A is meant to reach outside buyers such as the Compact: the record does not state it.
